evaluation_configuration.task_state_selection: Both runner versions use canonical task IDs, get_task_init_states(task_id), and initial_states[episode_idx] for episodes 0-49.
evaluation_configuration.benchmark_state_loader_note: The LIBERO checkout has a pre-existing local change to torch.load(..., weights_only=False) for trusted numpy init-state files. Its file timestamp is 2026-09-21, before both evaluations; it does not change task mapping or initial-state selection.
evaluation_configuration.noted_code_path_difference: The completion runner wraps predict_action in torch.inference_mode; the earlier runner relies on the model generation path. Both call predict_action with do_sample=False and use the same evaluation configuration.

configuration_mismatches: Training used double_quant=false, while both evaluation launches used the evaluator default double_quant=true. This is a measured configuration mismatch, not a demonstrated cause of the closed-loop result.
Local training used 3500 updates, effective batch 16, and 4-bit NF4; the official fine-tuning recipe uses 50000 steps, global batch 128, and no quantization.
The local training W&B token accuracy is a training-monitor metric; it is not held-out accuracy or LIBERO success rate.

An existing 24-frame official-checkpoint diagnostic is much stronger than the local adapter on those same training-distribution frames, and a separate official task0 control succeeds on 1/2 fixed states. These small controls support investigating local policy quality but do not replace the full-suite run or isolate a single cause.

historical_evidence_limits: The prior launch command and commit are recovered from its Codex session record; the prior log itself does not contain the full launch command.
The adapter path is identical in both launch commands. No adapter SHA-256 was captured at the prior launch; current digest and filesystem times are recorded separately.
The base repo ID was supplied to both offline launches. The resolved revision is supported by cached metadata that predates both runs, but was not printed into either launch log.
The completion runner adds an inference_mode wrapper; the generation call remains deterministic. This implementation difference is recorded rather than hidden.

limits: The 500-trial score is assembled by canonical task ID from separately parsed process logs; raw logs were never concatenated.

The prior run physically completed 382 rollouts. The completion prefix plus task-9 continuation executed 150 fresh rollouts, for 532 physical executions; only the old partial task-7 segment of 32 is excluded from the 500 scored trials.

The first completion process received SIGTERM (exit code 143) after 125 rollout records. Its log ends after task-9 state index 24 with no Python exception traceback; the separate continuation covers indices 25-49.
The old launch used the adapter path but did not record its SHA-256 at launch; the current digest and pre-run file timestamps are reported separately.
This is a single-seed, local 4-bit LoRA reproduction, not the official full-finetuned checkpoint or the paper's three-seed average.
The merge validates log arithmetic, task mapping, source hashes, and recorded configuration; it cannot recover runtime facts that were not recorded during the old launch.
